WITH net_fee_data AS (
  SELECT 
    orderslink,
    feerate - rebrate AS net_fee_rate,
    rebtotal
  FROM fees
),
per_order_stats AS (
  SELECT 
    orderslink,
    AVG(net_fee_rate) AS avg_net_fee_rate,
    AVG(rebtotal) AS avg_rebtotal
  FROM net_fee_data
  GROUP BY orderslink
),
overall_avg_net_fee AS (
  SELECT 
    AVG(net_fee_rate) AS overall_avg_net_fee_rate
  FROM net_fee_data
),
exceeding_orders AS (
  SELECT 
    pos.avg_net_fee_rate,
    pos.avg_rebtotal,
    (pos.avg_net_fee_rate - oaf.overall_avg_net_fee_rate) AS exceedance
  FROM per_order_stats pos
  CROSS JOIN overall_avg_net_fee oaf
  WHERE pos.avg_net_fee_rate > oaf.overall_avg_net_fee_rate
)
SELECT 
  AVG(avg_rebtotal) AS mean_avg_rebtotal,
  AVG(avg_net_fee_rate) AS mean_avg_net_fee_rate,
  AVG(exceedance) AS mean_exceedance
FROM exceeding_orders

assumptions.assumption: "Overall average net fee rate" is computed as the average of (feerate - rebrate) across all individual fee records in the fees table, treating each record equally. This provides a global baseline against which each order's average is compared.

alternatives.interpretation: "Overall average net fee rate" is computed as the average of the per-order average net fee rates, giving each order/group equal weight regardless of how many fee records it has.
